title: Crossing numbers of complete and complete bipartite graphs
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Zarankiewicz's formula cr(K_{m,n}) = floor(m/2) floor((m-1)/2) floor(n/2) floor((n-1)/2) and the Harary-Hill formula cr(K_n) = floor(n/2) floor((n-1)/2) floor((n-2)/2) floor((n-3)/2)/4, proved by OpenAI in 2026 for unrestricted drawings, with complete proofs. The first lesson defines drawings with continuous arcs and the crossing number, and proves the upper bound for K_{m,n} with Zarankiewicz's drawing. The second replaces every drawing by a normal one (polygonal, straight near vertices and crossings, no crossings of adjacent edges) with no more crossings. The third attaches to a normal drawing a bilinear form J on the edge space (signed crossing counts and half the order signs at common endpoints) and proves that J vanishes on pairs of cycles, by parallel copies, a formula for two chords of a disc and the zero signed intersection of closed polygonal walks. The fourth and fifth are algebra: Lagrange interpolation with barycentric weights and two interpolation problems on triangular patterns, and the inequality sum dim(U_i cap V_j) <= floor(m^2/4) N for subspaces with U_i cap V_i = 0, with its consequence for ranks of differences of matrices. The sixth proves Zarankiewicz's formula with an interpolation detector applied to the blocks of J, the seventh proves cr(K_n) >= Z(n) by evaluating symmetric polynomials at crossing pairs and showing that the image is injective and isotropic, and the eighth counts the crossings of the endpoint-sum two-page drawing.
prerequisites: core course Real Analysis I and II (Lebl, Basic Analysis I & II, version 6.3): Lemma 7.4.10 (Lebesgue covering lemma), Theorem 7.4.14 (Heine-Borel), Lemma 7.5.5, Theorem 7.5.6 and Theorem 8.5.1 (inverse function theorem)

core course Linear Algebra (Hefferon, Linear Algebra, fourth edition): Theorem Two.III.3.11, Theorem Three.II.2.14, Lemma Four.I.2.4, Definition Four.I.3.12, Corollary Four.I.3.16 and Theorem Four.II.1.5
core course Abstract Algebra I (Judson, Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications): Proposition 17.1.4 and Corollaries 17.2.3 and 17.2.4

checks.reading: The manuscripts 'The crossing number of complete bipartite graphs' and 'The crossing number of complete graphs' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026; local clone openai-math-20261006, TeX and compiled text) were read in full on 16 Oct 2026, and every step was checked while the lessons were written: the subspace intersection inequality (interpolation spaces, evaluation away from and at the nodes, the polynomial minors, rank loss at the nodes and the summation), the rank-sum corollary and its sharpness example, the cycle pairing (two chords of a disc, parallel copies, the coning argument), the additive block relation, the two-triangle interpolation lemmas for odd and even numbers of nodes, the rank detector and the order pairing, the lower bound for K_{m,n} with odd n and the deletion argument for even n, the polynomial cycle tests, the injectivity of the evaluation map and the isotropy argument for K_n, the axis drawing, the semicircle drawing with its genericity argument and the parity cases of the count, and the normalization of continuous-arc drawings. No error affecting a statement was found. Changes of form in the course: the cycle pairing is proved after subdividing every edge at its bends, so that parallel copies are parallel segments; the divisibility of the kernel polynomial for K_n by (x-y)(x-v)(u-y)(u-v) is derived by successive division by monic linear factors instead of unique factorization; the proper-crossing condition of the semicircle drawing is derived from the inverse function theorem; the remark that the lower-bound proofs bound the number of independent edge pairs with nonzero signed crossing count, in every normal drawing, is stated explicitly (Remark 5.3 and Remark 4.2 of the sixth and seventh lessons). The introduction of 'The crossing number of complete graphs' cites Aichholzer's heavily computer-assisted proof of cr(K_13) = 225 (CCCG 2021); Schaefer's survey, ninth edition of 17 July 2026, lists cr(K_13) among 219, 221, 223, 225 with an older reference; the first lesson cites both. Check program plan/checks_20261016/crossing_check.py (output crossing_check_run_20261016a.txt, 16 Oct 2026): 91,165 checks, 0 failures, all in exact rational arithmetic. The odd two-triangle interpolation for s = 1 to 6 and the even one for s = 2 to 5; the detector for n = 3, 5, 7 with all 6, 120 and 5,040 orders and for n = 9 with 40 random orders, together with its vanishing on additive and diagonal matrices and the rank one of its pieces; the order pairing for 2s = 4 and 6 with all orders and for 2s = 8 and 10 with 30 random orders; the subspace intersection inequality on 432 random coordinate and general cases with the sharp examples for m = 1 to 7, and the rank-sum inequality on 75 cases; the cycle pairing J(z,y) = 0 on a basis of the cycle space of 92 random drawings of K_4, K_5, K_6, K_{3,3}, K_{3,5} and K_{4,4}, straight, with bends and with added spikes (260 edge pairs crossing more than once, 88 crossing pairs with zero signed count), each with three choices of cuts; the block relation, R_ik = X_i - Y_k, the invertibility of R_ii and rank R_ik <= c_ik on axis drawings, random drawings and spiked drawings of K_{3,3}, K_{3,5}, K_{4,5}, K_{5,5}, K_{4,7}, K_{6,5}, with equality rank R_ik = c_ik and total 2 d_m d_n on the axis drawings; for K_5, K_7 and K_9 on two-page drawings with Z(n) crossings (also with spikes) and on random drawings: the polynomial cycle tests, the injectivity of the evaluation map, the isotropy of its image for the diagonal form, and |T| = 2 dim S on the two-page drawings; the crossing count of the endpoint-sum two-page drawing equal to Z(n) for n = 3 to 40, and the quadrant count of the axis drawing equal to d_m d_n for m, n <= 7.
checks.layout: at 375 px (16 Oct 2026): 8 lessons, 2,514 formulas typeset, no formula wider than the column, 0 MathJax errors, no horizontal page overflow; 73 formulas were set on several lines or rewritten after the first measurement, each tested beforehand with the site's MathJax

open_obligations: No named statement: every step is proved in the lessons or in the core courses listed as prerequisites.

The manuscripts report a formal verification in Lean (lean/docs/165.md of the OpenAI repository); the Lean files were not read and the verification scripts were not run, and the course does not depend on them.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
